one_month_reasoning: No confirmed Nebius event inside the window. The investor-events page lists no Q3 date; Q1/Q2 were reported May 13 / Aug 12, so mid-November is most likely, and I put ~15% on an in-window report (an unconfirmed Oct 22 estimate exists). Events in the window: (1) CME/NYMEX Silicon Data H100/B200 rental-index futures, targeted for 2026-10-05 (src 14). They give the first public forward curve for GPU rent. Spot indices are near highs (Ornn H100 $2.92, B200 $7.96 on Oct 1, src 7) but flat over 30 days (src 15), so I call this neutral. (2) Hyperscaler Q3 earnings and capex guides in the last week of October (dates are judgment). This is the largest sentiment swing for neoclouds and leans mildly positive given repeated upward capex revisions. (3) Possible ATM supply (up to 12.3M shares left at 6/30, src 1) and the 10Y at 5.29%, up ~30bp in a week (src 17), are mild headwinds. Net: close to symmetric. Median ~$230.5 (a hair below spot for ATM supply), lognormal sigma 28.5%: the usual ~28% monthly vol, nudged up for the small chance earnings land inside the window. P(>=spot) 0.49. Rounds 3-4: the GPU-life rebuild, the site-by-site model and the split discount rate change long-run cash flows, not anything inside the next month, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged. The AIB 50 MW lease (30-Sep) and the Meta/Microsoft delivery milestones are already public.

fair_value.method: Blend of a site-built cohort DCF ($188 12-month forward at split discount rates: IG contracted flows 8.5%, everything else WACC 12.8%; $184 at one rate) at 45%, 8.5x 2028E EBITDA of $12.5B ($257) at 35%, and 4.9x NTM EV/sales ($266) at 20%. Result ~$228, ~2% below spot (round 3: $206). The DCF rise ($140 -> $188) comes mostly from dropping the colo charge on owned campuses (F2), not from the split rate (+$4).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-built cohort FCFF model, Q4-2026 to 2035 plus steady-state terminal. Each of the 25 inventory sites is a layer with its own MW ramp, ownership and probability (sites.json, src 39). Signed contracts are explicit streams at their own terms: Microsoft 300 MW at Vineland, ~$3.48B/yr ($11.6M/MW) from Q4-26 to ~Apr-2031 (src 35); Meta-2025 $2.9B on 48 MW of Mantsala 1, to ~Dec-2030 (src 38); Meta-2026 dedicated $12B = 150 MW at $16M/MW, mid-2027 to mid-2032 (Mantsala 2 + Lappeenranta phase 1, src 36); Meta backstop on 190 MW at Lappeenranta from mid-2028, 85% of a $16.5M vintage price floored by Meta for 5 years (src 36); Q2-26 neolab deals 71 MW at $22.5M/MW for ~2.5 years at Bethune (src 1). Everything else (existing own-cloud fleet, uncontracted construction and pipeline) uses round 3's cohort engine: vintage yields $12M (<=2026), $13M 2027, $16.5M 2028-29, $15.5M 2030, $15M after; existing-fleet mix 80% ~2-yr / 20% on-demand (IG contracts now explicit); new vintages 30% 5-yr (unsigned) / 55% 2-yr / 15% on-demand; post-contract market index by age 1.00/0.70/0.52/0.45/0.41/0.37/0.33/0.29; 5-year economic life, refresh at 70% of unit capex, resale at 30% of CCIR levels. Costs (F2 fix): leased sites $2.5M per MW-yr power+colo and capex 75% of the $25M/MW unit (IT only; the host funds the shell); owned sites $1.1M per MW-yr (power $0.70M at $0.08/kWh + $0.4M site O&M) and capex 114% of unit ($17.5M IT + ~$11M facility). Overhead 39%->24% of revenue as round 3. Probability-weighted MW reach 3.7 GW in 2035 (2.76 GW owned): revenue $12.5B 2027, $25.9B 2028, $36.6B 2029, ~$44B 2031-33; EBITDA margin 49% 2027 -> 63% 2035. Tax 21%; WACC 12.8%, g 3%; terminal capex $11.5B > D&A. Single rate (all at 12.8%): EV $56.9B -> $184/share 12-month forward. Split rate: IG contracted flows (Microsoft, Meta) at 8.5%, Meta backstop floor at 9.5%, unrated Q2 deals at 11.0%, everything else at 12.8%: contracted PV rises $2.1B (IG $13.5B -> $14.9B; backstop $1.1B -> $1.75B; unrated $1.93B -> $1.97B) -> $188/share (contracted value rolled forward at ~9%, the rest at the 13.6% cost of equity). Bridge from round 3 ($140): site-by-site capacity with explicit contracts, round-3 costs -> $131 (3.7 GW probability-weighted by 2035 vs my old 4.8 GW, partly offset by faster owned-campus timing and a correct Q4-26 run-rate); leased capex IT-only -> $138; owned-site cost and capex (F2) -> $182; Meta backstop floor -> $184; split discounting -> $188. Sensitivities (single / split): life 4y 170/174, 6y 168/172, 7y 157/161; steep path 156/160, flat 252/256; ERP 4.65% 157/163, 5.0% 144/150; yield -10/+10% 130/134, 236/241; capex $22M/$28M 220/224, 146/151; owned cost $1.6M 160/164; owned capex 130% of unit 158/163; uncontracted-pipeline probabilities x0.7 156/160; no unnamed-gap layer 174/178; IG rate 7.5%/10% -> split 190/185; long-term mix 45%/15% 213/154; no resale 171/175.

inputs_detail.input: Capacity by site (replaces the aggregate GW path)
inputs_detail.value: 25 inventory sites + an unnamed ~0.7 GW gap layer (p 0.5); probability-weighted active MW ~0.55 GW Q4-26, ~1.3 GW 2027 avg, 3.7 GW 2035 (2.76 owned / 0.96 leased)
inputs_detail.derivation: Per-site MW and dates from the inventory (src 39) and its company sources (Q1-26 letter, src 37; Lappeenranta PR, src 40). Where sources conflict: Vineland 300 MW (Nebius PR) over 315/350 MW (secondary); Birmingham operational 2027 (Q1 letter) over Q4-26 energization (site page); Bethune treated as leased (Azur developer; not among the five owned sites in the Q1 letter). Undisclosed allocations are judgment: Longcross 15 MW (~9,000 B300), Newport 16 MW and UK fourth site 12 MW (GBP1.7B program = 65 MW across four sites less Harlow 22 and Longcross), Modi'in and Woodbury 5 MW each, Oklahoma 300 MW. Probabilities: 0.9-0.95 for leased construction (Bethune, Israel, Estonia, Harlow, AIB), 0.85 for the first phase of Independence/Highridge (power secured), 0.65-0.70 for later phases, 0.75 Birmingham (resident lawsuits), 0.7 unnamed UK site, 0.5 Oklahoma and the ~1 GW of the 5 GW contracted-power target not tied to a named site. Net of build capex and, through WACC, financing.

inputs_detail.input: Vintage contract yield and post-contract price path

The age index is fitted to rental history: SemiAnalysis H100 composite $6.62 (2H23) -> $3.34 (2Q25) = -50% in ~18 months, then flat ~$2.80 = ~0.42-0.44 at age 3 (src 24, 28); A100 at $0.93-1.58 = 23-39% of launch at ~6 years (src 7, 29, 28). Ornn spot puts A100/H100/B200 at ~equal $ per PFLOP-hr (src 7, 28), so old chips reprice with the falling cost of compute rather than to scrap. My index sits slightly below the 2026 H100 level because that evidence comes from a supply-constrained market.

inputs_detail.value: Leased: $2.5M per MW-yr power + colo; owned: $1.1M per MW-yr power + site O&M; overhead 39% (2026) -> 24% (2034+) of revenue; margin 49% 2027, 55% 2028, 63% 2035
inputs_detail.derivation: Research note: power $0.08/kWh (PUE included in the all-in draw) and colo ~$150/kW-month = ~$2.5M per MW-yr (src 28). Flag F2: owned sites (>75% of contracted power, src 37) should not pay colo on top of facility capex, so owned MW carry power ($0.70M) + $0.4M site O&M/insurance/property tax (judgment; Independence PILOT is only ~$0.03M/MW-yr, src 39). Overhead calibration unchanged from round 3 (Q2-26 AI-cloud 49.7% adj. EBITDA margin on mostly leased capacity, src 1).

inputs_detail.value: Unit $25M/MW in 2026, -3%/yr; owned sites 114% of unit (~$28.5M), leased 75% (~$18.75M, IT only); spent one year ahead of activation
inputs_detail.derivation: 2026 capex guide $20-25B for ~0.8-1.0 GW connected (src 1) gives the ~$25M blended unit. Leased hosts fund the shell (Mega Or ~$880M for 80 MW, Azur ~EUR1.5B, AIB with project debt; src 39), so Nebius pays IT plus fit-out. Owned: IT $17.5M + ~$11M facility (judgment; above the 30% facility share I used before so the F2 fix does not flatter owned sites). Sensitivity: owned 130% of unit -> $158/$163.

inputs_detail.value: Base economic life 5 years (refresh at age 5, 70% of unit capex); sensitivities 4/6/7 years; book D&A stays 5 years
inputs_detail.derivation: Nebius's accounting life is 5 years (4->5 from Jan-2026, src 2, 1). In the cohort model, with scarce power and new-vintage yields above aged-cohort market prices, refreshing at 5 years maximises value (4y $117, 5y $140, 6y $119, 7y $103): a MW holding a 6-7 year old GPU earns ~0.33-0.37 of a new vintage while bearing the same power and colo cost. Physical/cash life is longer (A100 contracted into 2029, src 25; cash-positive tail to ~7 years at $2.5M/MW cost), and I capture that tail through resale. The research note recommends 5 years as base for neoclouds (src 28), and Amazon's 6->5 cut for AI servers points the same way (src 30).

inputs_detail.value: $11.5B vs D&A ~$11.3B: GPUs 70% of unit / 5 yrs net of resale + facilities (owned 44% / leased 5% of unit) / 20 yrs + half of 3% growth
inputs_detail.derivation: Steady-state replacement of the 3.8 GW fleet at a 5-year economic life, net of resale at 30% x 26% of GPU capex (CCIR, src 23). Terminal capex stays at or above D&A, as the supervisor required.

inputs_detail.value: WACC 12.8% for uncontracted, post-contract, pipeline and terminal flows; 8.5% for Microsoft/Meta contracted flows; 9.5% Meta backstop floor; 11.0% unrated Q2-26 deals
inputs_detail.derivation: WACC: 10Y 5.29% (src 17) + beta 2.0 x ERP 4.14% (src 21) = 13.6% cost of equity, ~7% debt (src 22). Contracted IG rate: the only secured financing against such a contract is the $775M facility at SOFR+2.50% (src 33); SOFR 3.87% (src 32) gives 6.4% floating, and the 5-yr Treasury at 5.09% (src 31) puts a fixed-rate equivalent at ~7.6%. Meta's own 2031 notes at 4.55% (src 34) bound the pure credit piece (Microsoft Aaa, Meta Aa3; src 42, 41). The facility covers only the debt slice of capex, and the residual cash flows carry Nebius's delivery/termination risk (late-delivery discounts, Microsoft termination right), so I add ~0.9pt: 8.5%. Backstop floor 9.5%: Meta credit, but contingent and at undisclosed pre-agreed prices. Unrated neolab deals 11.0%: private counterparties, partly de-risked by prepayments covering 50-60% of capex (src 1). Contracted flows = contract revenue - site cost - 10% direct operating overhead - tax (with build-capex D&A shield) - build capex; the rest of corporate overhead stays at WACC.
Below nominal yields (src 17). Hated Moats uses 4% (src 12); I haircut for compute commoditisation. Sensitivity: 2% -> $141, 4% -> $160.

bear.story: GPU rents follow the steep path once Rubin supply arrives (post-contract ~0.3x within 3 years), new-deal yields fall ~10%, and the later phases of Independence, Highridge, Oklahoma and the unnamed capacity get delayed or cancelled (pipeline probabilities x0.7): site DCF ~$98 (split), ~$78 at a 5% ERP. Microsoft/Meta contracts hold (~$60/share of the split DCF), which floors the bear above round 3's $90. Funding gets expensive and multiples compress toward CoreWeave lows on ~400M shares.

base.story: Sites ramp on the inventory schedule: ~0.55 GW active in Q4-26, Meta dedicated tranches from mid-2027, Highridge 260 MW by Oct-2027, owned campuses carrying lower per-MW cost than colocation. 2027 revenue ~$12.3-12.5B with ~45-49% margins; ~25M more shares fund the build. GPU rents ease along the base index, the Microsoft/Meta contracts run to term, and the stock trades near ~8.5x forward EBITDA, close to the blended fair value.

bull.story: Scarcity lasts into 2028: re-contracting runs near original prices (flat-path site DCF ~$256), Meta's backstop clusters sell to third parties at full price, the full 1.2 GW at Independence and Highridge lands by 2030-32, and the market pays 10-12x 2028 EBITDA. Above ~$313-325 the $5.75B Aug-2026 notes convert (~17.7M shares), capping per-share upside a little.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$120 (about -48%) the market would most likely be pricing a fundamental failure, not 100%-vol noise. It is ~25% below the site DCF on the steep rental path ($156-160) and between that and the combined bear case (~$98), and below the $138.75 Sep-25 conversion price. Signs: GPU rental indices falling toward ~0.3x launch within 2-3 years of each generation; mid-term contracts re-leasing well below original prices; new deals below ~$12M/MW; a delivery failure that triggers Microsoft's termination right or Meta's late-delivery discounts; Highridge missing 260 MW by Oct-2027 or Independence power slipping past 2029; or financing markets closing. Raised from $110 because the contracted Microsoft/Meta streams (~$60/share in the split DCF) and the lower owned-site costs lift the steep-path value.

GPU economic life and post-contract price path: 5/6/7-year life gives a split DCF of $188/172/161; steep vs flat rental decay gives $160 vs $256
Owned-campus economics (F2): the DCF depends on owned MW costing ~$1.1M/MW-yr plus ~$11M/MW of facility capex; owned cost $1.6M or facility capex 30% higher each takes ~$24 off

Delivery on the big owned campuses: Independence and Highridge (1.2 GW each) and Birmingham (lawsuits) are ~$74/share of value on probabilities of 0.65-0.85; later phases depend on utility power by 2029
Re-leasing risk: ~55% of capacity sits on ~2-year mid-term contracts, so 2028-29 renewals reprice to the market index; only the Microsoft/Meta 5-year deals are long-dated
2027 capex size and funding mix (equity/convert dilution vs prepayments and secured debt); Q3 ATM usage unknown
Execution on >1GW/yr deployment: power, construction, GPU delivery
Customer concentration (Meta, Microsoft, a few neolabs) and AI-lab credit quality
Rates and ERP: 10Y 5.29%, 5Y 5.09%; ERP 4.14% / 4.65% / 5.0% moves the split DCF $188 / $163 / $151; the contracted rate (7.5-10%) moves it only $185-190
reasoning: Round 4 makes two fixes Kilian asked for. (1) Sites: the DCF is now built from the 25-site inventory. Each site is one layer with its own ramp, ownership and probability. Signed contracts are explicit streams at their own price and dates: Microsoft at Vineland, Meta-2025 on Mantsala 1, Meta-2026 dedicated on Mantsala 2 + Lappeenranta, the Meta backstop on Lappeenranta, and the Q2 neolab deals at Bethune. They no longer sit inside a 30% IG share of every vintage. Uncontracted construction and pipeline are probability-weighted, net of capex. The F2 flag (colo charged on owned MW that also carry facility capex) was the largest change. Owned campuses now carry $1.1M/MW-yr and ~$28.5M/MW capex, and leased sites $2.5M/MW-yr and IT-only capex. The F3 backstop is a floor on 190 MW. The F7 timing lag is fixed: Highridge and Independence follow company dates. Total probability-weighted MW is lower than my old path, 3.7 GW in 2035 vs 4.8. Bridge: $140 -> $131 (site layout) -> $138 (leased capex) -> $182 (owned costs) -> $184 (backstop). (2) Discounting: IG contracted flows at 8.5%, anchored on the $775M facility at SOFR+2.50% (SOFR 3.87%, 5Y 5.09%) plus a delivery-risk premium. The backstop floor is at 9.5%, unrated deals at 11%, and the rest at WACC 12.8%. The split adds only ~$4 ($184 -> $188), because the contracts are at most 5 years long and much of their early cash goes to build capex. Most of the value is in uncontracted capacity and the terminal value, which stay at WACC. Blend 45/35/20 unchanged, multiples unchanged: fair value $228 (round 3 $206). Scenarios: bear $100 / base $228 / bull $410 at 25/50/25. The bear is floored a bit higher by the contracted streams; the bull adds the backstop sold at full price and the full owned build. Ladder: same construction (equal blend of the scenario lognormal mixture and a single lognormal, median $224, 80% sigma), giving P(>=232) 0.479 (round 3 0.442). Thesis break $110 -> $120. The 1-month ladder is unchanged. Limits: the per-MW split of owned vs leased costs and Meta-2026 $/MW are judgment. Several site MW figures are undisclosed (Longcross, Newport, UK fourth site, Oklahoma, Modi'in, Woodbury). The 20-F property table could not be read in full. Overhead is still calibrated on round-2 margins.

gpu_life.note: Nebius self-operates its GPU cloud (company life 5 years, fact-checked against the FY25 20-F), so the research applies fully. Split-rate DCF 4y 175 / 5y 188 / 6y 172 / 7y 162; single-rate 184 at 5y. A 5-year refresh still maximises value because power, not GPUs, is the binding constraint. The price path matters more than the life: steep $160, flat $256 (split). Contract terms now match the actual contracts, and the 5-year Microsoft/Meta terms coincide with the 5-year refresh.

discounting.basis: IG contracted (Microsoft Aaa, Meta Aa3) 8.5%: Nebius's $775M facility secured on an IG contract is SOFR+2.50%, i.e. 6.4% floating at SOFR 3.87% and ~7.6% fixed-equivalent at the 5Y Treasury 5.09%. Meta's own 2031 notes at 4.55% bound the pure credit piece. I add ~0.9pt for Nebius delivery and termination risk on the equity slice. Meta backstop floor 9.5% (contingent, undisclosed prices). Unrated Q2-26 neolab deals 11.0% (private counterparties, prepayments cover 50-60% of capex). Uncontracted, post-contract, pipeline and terminal flows at WACC 12.8%. Contracted flows = contract revenue - site cost - 10% direct overhead - tax - build capex; contracted PV is rolled forward at ~9%, the rest at the 13.6% cost of equity.
